pr_title: Fix the desync related to owner changes
pr_body:
Closes #19930.

"[Serialize the actor generation for network orders](https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/20084/commits/b961b700ae214f9a08002836da8d80fd58be0b8b)" is the commit with the relevant changes.

Explanation:
`Target` has an internal `type` field, which is used for order serialization (via `Target.SerializableType`). This field is readonly which means a target of type `Actor` always has that `SerializableType` locked in as `TargetType.Actor`. `Target.Type` however is not locked, and does not necessarily return the readonly `type`. For example, when the actor generation is changed, `TargetType.Invalid` is returned no matter what `type` is.
We did not serialize (and deserialize) the actor generation and thus did not send it over the network with the orders. Since our network changes, orders are no longer serialized and deserialized for the client issuing them.
That means that an order can be send with a target that is or becomes invalid for the local client (due to the generation changing), but remains valid for other receiving clients (since they do not know about the generation change). Obviously having one client with an invalid target while the other one(s) have a valid target does not play well with syncing.

If this fix is not enough, we can always fall back to just serializing and deserializing local orders again.

Removing `SerializableType` and the likes is an idea for a follow-up, but not needed for this fix.

Testcase:
Included in a separate commit which adds `ChangeOwnerWarhead`s. I usually start an 8 AI game with two teams on max speed and max starting units with two spectating clients. Without the fix it usually desyncs within at least 5 minutes.
pr_comments:
I suggest reviewing with whitespace changes hidden: https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/20084/files?w=1
The switch-case statement had weird formatting which caused VS 2022 to always change indentation whenever I typed, so I fixed that in a separate commit before the actual fix.
Update: Maybe this is not enough, https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/blob/bleed/OpenRA.Game/Network/Order.cs#L339 might need changing too since I can still trigger an occasional desync.
Updated. Sometimes an incorrect actor generation was serialized, which is fixed now by directly using the generation held by the target.

issue_context.title: Out of sync crash relating to owner change
issue_context.body:
As far as I can tell this happens due to this commit: https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/commit/6421c1751546ad275e4e00546a78046761c45ce2

CA has a few weapons that change the target actor to Neutral. It doesn't crash immediately, but after a few minutes, an out of sync crash occurs which only causes one client to crash (so only that client has a sync log generated).

Seems to happen due to owner changes more broadly (as it also happened after I removed weapons that change actors to Neutral, I think due to mind control units still being present, which also use ChangeOwner()).

Example of the exception:

```OpenRA engine version {DEV_VERSION}
Red Alert mod version {DEV_VERSION}
on map 4070a9a020bcd8a5f1f85cb18eb4c2afda47398b (Mass Confliction by Nuke'm Bro.).
Date: 2022-02-05 18:51:55Z
Operating System: Windows (Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19043.0)
Runtime Version: .NET CLR 6.0.1
Exception of type `System.InvalidOperationException`: Out of sync in frame 1561.
 Compare syncreport.log with other players.
   at OpenRA.Network.OrderManager.OutOfSync(Int32 frame) in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Network\OrderManager.cs:line 77
   at OpenRA.Network.OrderManager.ReceiveSync(ValueTuple`3 sync) in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Network\OrderManager.cs:line 155
   at OpenRA.Network.NetworkConnection.OpenRA.Network.IConnection.Receive(OrderManager orderManager) in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Network\Connection.cs:line 309
   at OpenRA.Sync.<>c__DisplayClass13_0.<RunUnsynced>b__0() in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Sync.cs:line 167
   at OpenRA.Sync.RunUnsynced[T](Boolean checkSyncHash, World world, Func`1 fn) in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Sync.cs:line 205
   at OpenRA.Sync.RunUnsynced(World world, Action fn) in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Sync.cs:line 168
   at OpenRA.Game.InnerLogicTick(OrderManager orderManager) in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Game.cs:line 623
   at OpenRA.Game.LogicTick() in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Game.cs:line 638
   at OpenRA.Game.Loop() in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Game.cs:line 803
   at OpenRA.Game.Run() in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Game.cs:line 856
   at OpenRA.Game.InitializeAndRun(String[] args) in J:\ora\OpenRA.Game\Game.cs:line 294
   at OpenRA.Launcher.Program.Main(String[] args) in J:\ora\OpenRA.Launcher\Program.cs:line 32
```

Orignally replicated by adding this class: https://github.com/darkademic/CAmod/blob/master/OpenRA.Mods.CA/Warheads/ChangeOwnerToNeutralWarhead.cs

Then changing M1Carbine to use this warhead.

```salt
	Warhead@DriverKill: ChangeOwnerToNeutral
		ValidTargets: Vehicle
		ValidRelationships: Enemy
		Range: 0c511
```

But have since tried with the standard ChangeOwnerWarhead and that also replicates the issue.

```salt
	Warhead@c: ChangeOwner
		Duration: 0
		ValidRelationships: Enemy
		Range: 0c511
		ValidTargets: Vehicle
```

review_comments: We have `UIntFromActor()` just above for the sole purpose of making a null check; this should probably get a null check as well?

We create a new `Target` here from the actor with the generation we were told to use, but at this point the actor's generation could have changed. I guess you're relying on the targeting code later dropping the target because of that mismatch, but spitballing here, why not:
Add an (optional) `generation` parameter to `Order.TryGetActorFromUInt()` and maybe even `World.GetActorById()` and pass the generation you just read. If an actor is found but the generation doesn't match, pretend no actor is found and save us some trouble with a target that we know will eventually be invalid.
*(alternatively you can check the generation here after getting the actor and still not create a `Target`, but I like my first suggestion better)*

This would take us back to square one wrt the local and remote clients having different target states!

I don't necessarily disagree with the motivation, but if we're going to change this it should be done as part of a larger rewrite instead of adding yet another edge case that could go wrong.

Why have different? The serialized order includes the targeted generation and then on the receiving end we make sure to ***only create a `Target` if that is the current generation*** 🤔   Maybe I'm missing something ... would the ***generations*** differ between clients?

The sending client would have a target that is internally an actor but returns `TargetType.Invalid` while the receiving client would have a target that is internally `TargetType.Invalid`. We haven't yet proved that there aren't more cases where this distinction matters.

Hm ok I guess that makes sense.
I figured the sending client would recreate its target based on the incoming order. Did we use to do that and change it as part of the netcode rewrite or am I going crazy? Anyway, that's a valid explanation of what I was missing.

> Did we use to do that and change it as part of the netcode rewrite

Yes, 6421c1751546ad275e4e00546a78046761c45ce2 (second point).

> Did we use to do that and change it as part of the netcode rewrite or am I going crazy?

Yes we did use to do that because orders would get serialized and deserialized even for the local client, i.e. when they never need to go over the network. That was changed to not serializing and deserializing to save the unnecessary overhead.
